assistantMessage.text:
Confirmed: doc comment says "Takes qty units if that many are left" — meaning it should succeed when `have == qty` (taking the last units). The condition `have <= qty` incorrectly fails that case.All 7 tests pass.

**Bug:** In `reserve(sku, qty)`, the doc comment says it should "take `qty` units if that many are left" — i.e., it should succeed even when exactly `qty` units remain (taking the last ones). The code used `have <= qty` as the failure condition, which incorrectly rejected the exact-match case (e.g., reserving the last 3 units when stock is 3 would fail).

**Fix** (`/tmp/vcmp/w/t2/src/inventory.ts`):

```4:5:/tmp/vcmp/w/t2/src/inventory.ts
	const have = stock.get(sku) ?? 0;
	if (have < qty) { return false; }
```

(changed `<=` to `<`)

**Tests:** `npm test` now passes all 7 tests, including `reserve can take the last units`, which previously would have failed under the buggy `<=` check.

assistantMessage.text:
The bug is confirmed: the doc comment on `checkout` states it should throw `'out of stock <sku>'` when a reservation fails, but the implementation just `continue`s, silently ignoring the failure.All tests pass (7/7), including `checkout throws when out of stock`.

**The bug:** In `checkout()`, the doc comment says it "throws `'out of stock <sku>'` when one can't be [reserved]", but the loop body did:

```typescript
if (!reserve(sku, qty)) { continue; }
```

This silently skipped the failed reservation instead of throwing, so checkout would return a total even when an item was unavailable.

**The fix** (only `src/checkout.ts` changed):

```typescript
if (!reserve(sku, qty)) { throw new Error(`out of stock ${sku}`); }
```

**Test result:** `npm test` → all 7 tests pass, 0 failures, including `checkout throws when out of stock`.
